cohort_statement: This synthetic Lab 1 dataset represents 100 students across 8 questions. It contains 757 records of one student's work on one question; 283 included at least one tutor question.
summary_sentences: A notable pattern in this synthetic lab data is the frequent use of the tutor for validation after passing autograder checks and for direct answers before attempting code.
The professor can inspect individual student journeys to observe the sequence of events around these tutor interactions.

findings.headline: Validation Questions After Passing Autograder Varied by Question
findings.explanation: Students used the tutor for validation after successfully passing the autograder. This behavior was observed more often for some questions than others.
findings.instructor_prompt: How do question characteristics relate to the frequency of validation requests after a passing autograder check?

facts.title: Validation questions after passing the autograder
facts.evidence: Question 1.1.5 had the highest share classified as validation after passing the autograder (13 of 38 (34.2%)); Question 3.2 had the lowest (8 of 36 (22.2%)).
facts.caution: These purposes were classified by Gemini from each complete student-question record. They remain model interpretations.

The student passed the autograder before using the tutor; no code change was recorded after the reply. 2 code runs and 1 tutor question were recorded. A passing autograder check was recorded.

findings.headline: Direct Answer Requests Showed Differences Across Questions
findings.explanation: Direct-answer requests before editing or running code were recorded, with some questions receiving more of these requests than others.
findings.instructor_prompt: What characteristics of certain questions are associated with a higher rate of direct-answer requests before any code attempt?

facts.title: Direct-answer requests by question
facts.evidence: Question 3.2 had the highest share classified as a direct-answer request before editing or running code (11 of 36 (30.6%)); Question 1.1.1 had the lowest (4 of 26 (15.4%)).
facts.caution: These purposes were classified by Gemini from each complete student-question record. They remain model interpretations.

findings.headline: Debugging Questions After Problems Differed by Question
findings.explanation: Debugging questions after an error or failed autograder check were recorded, with the frequency varying across different questions.
findings.instructor_prompt: What question characteristics are associated with a higher incidence of debugging questions after a problem is recorded?

facts.title: Debugging questions after recorded problems
facts.evidence: Question 3.3 had the highest share classified as debugging after an error or failed autograder check (9 of 43 (20.9%)); Question 1.1.1 had the lowest (0 of 26 (0.0%)).
facts.caution: These purposes were classified by Gemini from each complete student-question record. They remain model interpretations.

findings.headline: Post-Tutor Reply Code Activity Varied
findings.explanation: After a tutor reply, some records showed no subsequent code change, while others involved using exact tutor code, sometimes followed by further edits.
findings.instructor_prompt: How do the different types of tutor replies relate to whether students make subsequent code changes or use the provided code directly?

facts.title: What followed tutor replies
facts.evidence: 140 of 283 tutor-using records (49.5%) had no later recorded code change; 53 of 283 tutor-using records (18.7%) had a later edit without exact tutor code; 55 of 283 tutor-using records (19.4%) used exact tutor code without a later edit; 35 of 283 tutor-using records (12.4%) used exact tutor code and later edited.

caveats: This is synthetic scenario data. It does not estimate how real DSC 10 students behave.
Recorded events describe actions, not intent, understanding, learning, or tutor effectiveness.
A passing autograder check shows that recorded tests passed; it does not establish learning or independent authorship.
Gemini's student-question purpose classifications agreed with 86.2% of the generator's synthetic labels.
